_comment: Where each finding family is remediated: Book 11, Chapter 08's finding-family table (docs/books/b11-zero-trust/08-close-before-you-assess.md#finding-families), with the identity risk triage row the Zero Trust Assessment guide adds. Each family names the workbook page that remediates it, the evidence that shows a finding is ready for closure, the owner (Book 11, Chapter 07's pillar owners), the attack the gap enables, what the fix depends on, and the NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls the remediation supports. 'tests' routes a Zero Trust Assessment 3.1.0 test ID to a family; 'categories' routes the tool's TestCategory when the ID isn't listed, and the register marks that match as by category so someone confirms it. A finding that matches neither is 'unrouted': it goes to the program lead to assign. The routing is design guidance; it says where the work lives, not that a page closes anything.

emergency-access.title: Emergency access
emergency-access.attackPath: A tenant lockout during an outage, or an emergency account used by an attacker with nobody alerted
emergency-access.ready: Two cloud-only emergency accounts with phishing-resistant credentials, excluded from blocking Conditional Access; the sign-in alert fired on a test sign-in; the quarterly validation record

standing-privilege.title: Standing privilege and PIM
standing-privilege.attackPath: A stolen administrator session or token reaches standing privileged roles without an activation, approval or alert
standing-privilege.ready: The PIM role-setting export; no active permanent assignment outside the exception register; an activation test with its approval and audit record

phishing-resistant-admin.title: Phishing-resistant admin authentication
phishing-resistant-admin.attackPath: An administrator's password and phishable second factor relayed through an adversary-in-the-middle page
phishing-resistant-admin.ready: The authentication strength policy export; registration report for every privileged user; a test sign-in refused without a phishing-resistant method

conditional-access.title: Conditional Access gaps
conditional-access.attackPath: Sign-ins that skip the policy a risky user, legacy client or stolen token should have met
conditional-access.ready: The policy export from the library; report-only results reviewed; the policy enforced with its exclusions registered; a test sign-in blocked as designed

app-secrets.title: Application secrets
app-secrets.owner: Application owners, with the platform teams
app-secrets.attackPath: A client secret copied from code, a pipeline or a laptop, used to sign in as the application
app-secrets.ready: The credential inventory with no secret outside the exception register; the app management policy export; each moved workload signing in with a managed identity or certificate

ownerless-apps.title: Ownerless privileged applications
ownerless-apps.owner: Application owners, with the platform teams
ownerless-apps.attackPath: A highly privileged application nobody watches, abused for persistence or data access
ownerless-apps.ready: The application governance record with an owner for every privileged application; the owner report showing none missing

redirect-uri.title: Redirect URI risk
redirect-uri.owner: Application owners, with the DNS/DDI team
redirect-uri.attackPath: A token sent to a redirect URI whose domain or host an attacker can claim
redirect-uri.ready: The redirect URI inventory reconciled to owned DNS zones; no dangling or insecure URI outside the exception register

device-compliance.title: Device compliance gaps
device-compliance.attackPath: Corporate data reached from an unmanaged or noncompliant device
device-compliance.ready: Compliance policy exports; the device-based Conditional Access policy enforced; a noncompliant test device refused

endpoint-hardening.title: Endpoint hardening gaps
endpoint-hardening.attackPath: Malware or an exploit that runs on an endpoint no rule, sensor or block mode stops
endpoint-hardening.ready: Onboarding coverage report; ASR rules and prevention settings in block mode with their exclusions registered; a test detection that raised its alert

network-access.title: Network access gaps
network-access.attackPath: Traffic that reaches private or internet resources without passing an identity-aware policy point
network-access.ready: Forwarding profile and policy exports; traffic logs showing the in-scope population routed; a blocked test destination

ddos-waf-exposure.title: DDoS, WAF and public exposure
ddos-waf-exposure.attackPath: An internet-facing service exhausted or exploited because nothing absorbs or inspects the traffic
ddos-waf-exposure.ready: The public exposure register; DDoS protection and WAF in prevention mode on every in-scope endpoint; a blocked test request in the WAF log

labels.title: No labels, defaults or containers
labels.owner: Data owners and the data office
labels.attackPath: Sensitive files and mail that carry no label, so no policy follows them
labels.ready: The label and label policy exports; default and container labels published; label activity in the audit log

rights-management.title: Rights Management and mail encryption
rights-management.owner: Data owners and the data office
rights-management.attackPath: A labeled file or message read by whoever ends up holding it
rights-management.ready: The Rights Management service activation state; encrypting labels published; a protected test message opened only by its recipient

audit-visibility.title: Audit and visibility gaps
audit-visibility.attackPath: Activity nobody can reconstruct because its log was never sent or kept
audit-visibility.ready: Diagnostic settings exports; the workspace receiving every expected table; the telemetry-completeness check passing

identity-risk-triage.title: Identity risk triage
identity-risk-triage.attackPath: A compromised account that ID Protection flagged and nobody triaged
identity-risk-triage.ready: The risky-user and risky-sign-in detections deployed; the daily triage record; no high-risk user older than the triage window
